questions: Do the iteration 8 metrics match iteration 6 (score 36.3097) to four decimals? If so, geometry is exhausted, and the pipeline and controller should be the focus.
Does line_loss_events fall below one on the oval or s-bend, and does max_error drop below 0.06 m on any track?
Did the Integrator scale the sensor weights to the wider ±0.04 m row, and does the signal saturate at the outer sensors?
Per track, at what step and progress does the first line loss begin, and does steering_oscillation rise on the slalom?

intent: Revert mass to 0.8 kg, the best-scoring setting, and test whether a wider ±0.04 m row of 16 mm sensors removes the early line loss on the oval and s-bend. Expect line_loss_events below one and max_error at or below 0.06 m on those tracks. Because the controller weights must match the new spacing, the Integrator should scale them to x/0.03 relative to the ±0.03 layout.
learning: Mass 0.5 kg changed only the slalom (progress down, max_error down, oscillation down) and reduced the score, so mass 0.8 kg stays. Sensor visibility at 16 mm with ±0.03 m reaches about 0.0505 m of offset, short of the 0.06 m limit, so ±0.04 m is the last geometry test on line-loss reach. If it moves nothing, the next levers are controller damping (kd) and base_speed.
rationale:
Iteration 7 (mass 0.5 kg) left the oval and s-bend unchanged: max_error 0.0612 and 0.0616 m, one line-loss event per trial, and no finishes. On the slalom, max_error fell to 0.0618 m and steering_oscillation fell to 0.1435, but progress dropped from 0.110 to 0.105 and the score fell from 36.31 to 35.64. Mass therefore does not lift the off-track floor and is not the lever to keep. Iteration 6 (mass 0.8 kg, kp 3.0) remains the best-scoring platform.

The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.12/4) = 0.06 m, and body_width cannot change that. The sensor footprint and row are the remaining geometry that sets when the line is lost. A 16 mm sensor at x = ±0.03 m sees tape only out to about 0.0505 m of robot offset, so line loss begins before the 0.06 m limit. Moving the outer sensors to x = ±0.04 m extends that reach to about 0.0605 m, just past the limit. This is the one geometry change not yet tested with a 16 mm footprint, and it is the only one that targets the line-loss mechanism directly. Iteration 1 widened the spread at 12 mm and gave identical metrics, so I expect the change to be small. I therefore revert mass to 0.8 kg, keep the iteration-6 body and wheels, and widen the spread to ±0.04 m with five sensors at 0.02 m spacing. The Integrator must scale the weights to match. Expected result: line_loss_events fall toward zero on the oval and s-bend, and max_error stays near 0.060 m. If the metrics match iteration 6 again, geometry is exhausted and the Integrator should move to kd and base_speed.
